status: NOT RUN — requires separate approval for new role credentials and first Cloud installation

impact.classification: First installation into an empty GroundZero namespace, not deletion/recreation of existing Cloud GroundZero data.
impact.existing_groundzero_data_loss: No GroundZero schema, roles, objects or SQLx history found at the inspected snapshot. Recheck immediately before installation; stop on any difference.
impact.backup: No existing GroundZero data to back up at this snapshot. Managed auth/storage and platform data are outside scope; Dashboard backup existence and recoverability remain NOT VERIFIED. This is not a decision to forgo backup of any pre-existing data.
excluded: new credential generation before explicit approval
impact.synthetic_data: Approved smoke tests would create new synthetic users, sessions, workspaces, documents, revisions and audit/queue rows. They remain after testing; no automatic schema/drop/truncate cleanup.

preconditions: Confirm exact project-ref, TLS-verified session host:5432, postgres database and authenticated current_user=postgres match the inventory.
Require no fvoci schema, no fvoci_migrator/fvoci_app roles, no fvoci-owned objects outside that schema, and no GroundZero SQLx history. Unexpected objects or role sharing stop initialization.
Record managed schemas/owners/ACLs and public objects before installation for after-state comparison; exclude transient connection counts.
Receive explicit approval to create the standard two roles, two unique credentials and a named private retention mechanism. Do not reuse the admin password or deploy/ public test passwords.

Build reviewed source and selected test binaries before credential injection. Pin manual execution to reviewed immutable SHA and repository owner. Keep full URLs/passwords/CA contents out of logs and artifacts.
Continue verify-full TLS with existing CA; do not lower TLS verification, grant new permanent admin capabilities, or switch to transaction pooler.
additional_existing_secret_note: SUPABASE_TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL_SESSION_POOLER reportedly exists but was neither read nor needed for inventory. Any use must validate the same target and enforce verify-full with the existing CA; never print its value.

bootstrap: DATABASE_ADMIN_URL (derived privately from the validated existing admin target)
migrate: DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL (standard fvoci_migrator session login, same approved target, new credential)
smoke: DATABASE_URL (fvoci_app session login, same target, NOBYPASSRLS)

planned_commands: fvoci-server db migrate (repeat to confirm unchanged one-row SQLx ledger/checksum)
Optional approved normal-delete/restore smoke: cargo test --locked --package fvoci-server --test trash deleted_documents_disappear_and_come_back_with_their_subtree -- --exact --test-threads=1
execution_notes: Run only explicitly selected first_flow/db_context binaries against this confirmed empty dedicated test target. Do not point cargo xtask test, full workspace tests, FreshDb fixtures or backup tests at Cloud.

first_flow verifies create/read/update, idempotent saves, app role identity, NOBYPASSRLS, unauthorized visibility/update denial and direct DELETE permission denial. db_context verifies user context clears after commit/rollback.

first_flow/db_context alone do not prove a successful application delete; the named existing trash test adds soft-delete/access-denial/restore of its own new synthetic document subtree, if approved as part of smoke scope.
The Cloud session route for migrator and custom app roles is not established by administrator connection success; each role must connect itself and its real commands/tests must pass.
Record final source SHA, SQL SHA256/SQLx checksum, role properties, actual route, selected test names/results and managed-object before/after equality.
If bootstrap or migrate fails, preserve any partial/new GroundZero state and report the failure; do not retry with broader permissions or automatic cleanup.
No restore, old backup compatibility, real Cloud OIDC, full Cloud integration suite or browser flow is claimed by these selected DB/API smoke tests.

For any future approved backup containing real data, use encrypted backup plus approved private storage and integrity/restore checks; never publish plaintext backup through public repository artifacts.
